Read mortality data from a long-format table

Source: R/data_loading.R
read_mortality.Rd

The primary entry point for loading mortality data into mortensor. Accepts any long-format data.frame or data.table containing mortality rates (or death counts + population) with columns for year, age, and optionally one or more stratification variables (e.g. sex, region, deprivation).

Usage

read_mortality(
  dt,
  mx_col = NULL,
  ages,
  years = NULL,
  group_cols = NULL,
  pop_col = NULL,
  deaths_col = NULL,
  cause = NULL,
  age_labels = NULL,
  year_col = "year",
  age_col = "age_group"
)

Arguments

dt

A data.frame or data.table in long format.

mx_col

Character name of the mortality-rate column. Either mx_col or both deaths_col and pop_col must be provided.

ages

Integer vector of age-group start values (e.g. c(30, 35, 40, 90)), in the same order used to sort the age column.

years

Integer vector of calendar years to keep (default: all in dt).

group_cols

Character vector of column names defining groups/strata (e.g. c("sex", "region")). If NULL, auto-detected as all columns that are not year_col, age_col, mx_col, deaths_col, or pop_col.

pop_col

Optional character name of a population-exposure column. Required when using deaths_col.

deaths_col

Optional character name of a death-count column. If provided together with pop_col, mortality rates are computed as deaths / population.

cause

Optional cause-of-death label (e.g. "IHD").

age_labels

Optional character vector of age-group labels (e.g. c("30-34", "35-39")). If NULL, labels are derived from ages.

year_col

Character name of the year column (default "year").

age_col

Character name of the age column (default "age_group").

Value

A mort_data object.

Expected input format

A long-format table with one row per year x age x group combination. Required columns (names configurable):

Year column

Integer calendar year (e.g. 2001, 2002). Specify via year_col.

Age column

Age-group identifier, either a label like "30-34" or an integer start age like 30. Specify via age_col.

Rate column or deaths + population columns

Either a single column of pre-computed mortality rates (specify via mx_col), or two columns: one for death counts (deaths_col) and one for population exposure (pop_col), in which case mx = deaths / population is computed internally.

Group columns (optional)

Any additional columns that define strata (e.g. "sex", "region"). Specify via group_cols. If NULL, age_col and year_col are auto-detected and all remaining non-value columns are treated as group columns.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Minimal example - rates already computed, single stratum
dt <- data.table::data.table(
  year      = rep(2001:2020, each = 13),
  age_group = rep(seq(30, 90, 5), 20),
  mx        = runif(260, 0.001, 0.05)
)
md <- read_mortality(dt, mx_col = "mx", ages = seq(30, 90, 5))

# With deaths + population, two strata
dt2 <- data.table::data.table(
  year   = rep(2001:2020, each = 26),
  age    = rep(rep(seq(30, 90, 5), each = 2), 20),
  sex    = rep(c("Male", "Female"), 260),
  deaths = rpois(520, 50),
  pop    = rpois(520, 10000)
)
md2 <- read_mortality(dt2, deaths_col = "deaths", pop_col = "pop",
                      ages = seq(30, 90, 5), age_col = "age",
                      group_cols = "sex")
} # }
